text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen 1.2% today and 18.5% over two weeks, a sharp decline that accelerated after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 3rd. The stock has lost ground each of the last four trading days, suggesting investors reacted negatively to the financial results or the outlook the company provided alongside them — though the specific details from that earnings report aren't available here to confirm the exact driver.

The broader refining environment offers limited support: oil prices remain solid (US crude near $100/barrel), and refineries are running at a healthy 94.5% capacity, which should be supporting margins. However, recent political news — including comments from the U.S. Secretary of State on November 9th about stalled Iran negotiations — may have cooled some investor appetite for energy stocks, adding headwind to a stock already under pressure from company-specific news.
